With the proposal cost fixed at 6, continued support yields a payoff of -4. The coalition therefore decided to withdraw its support.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Its private commercial assessments remain confidential.","candidate_implication":"Researchers should predict that internal records surrounding withdrawals will discuss deteriorating competitive gains more often than changes in expected alternative regulation, while public statements will omit the underlying commercial quantities.","derivation":"Under CA, the support decision responds to incremental competitive benefit net of the common proposal cost. The notice is private, and commercial numbers are not publicly disclosed. Jointly, these premises predict an internal–public asymmetry in explanations, especially when support changes.","extra_assumption":"Researchers can access a sufficiently large collection of internal and public documents generated under comparable decisions."},{"id":"discovery_CA_02_02","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The day-10 notice lowered the expected burden of alternative carbon regulation from 12 to 2. Our incremental competitive benefit remains 12. Under the competitive-advantage criterion, net support value is therefore 12 minus the proposal cost of 6, or 6. The coalition decided to continue supporting the proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Confidential commercial estimates are not being released.","candidate_implication":"Researchers should predict that some internal records will acknowledge large revisions in anticipated alternative-regulation burdens without recording any corresponding change in endorsement.","derivation":"Under CA, endorsement depends on incremental competitive benefit rather than the expected burden of alternative regulation. A notice affecting only the latter leaves the calculated support payoff unchanged, apart from the independent reversal error.","extra_assumption":"Internal records routinely identify which assessment changed."},{"id":"discovery_CA_02_03","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The reliable private notice revised the coalition’s incremental competitive benefit downward from 12 to 2. Subtracting the proposal cost of 6 gives a continued-support payoff of -4. Consistent with that assessment, the coalition decided not to support the proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition has withdrawn its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal. No private commercial figures are disclosed.","candidate_implication":"Across comparable episodes, researchers should predict a discontinuous increase in withdrawal language in internal documents when revised competitive-benefit estimates fall below the proposal cost, rather than a smooth response to changes of any size.","derivation":"CA defines payoff as competitive benefit minus proposal cost, and the coalition normally supports exactly when that payoff is nonnegative. Together these premises create a decision threshold at a competitive benefit of 6; the small reversal probability adds occasional exceptions.","extra_assumption":"Comparable records include competitive-benefit estimates on both sides of the cost threshold."},{"id":"discovery_CA_02_04","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: Yesterday’s notice reduced the expected incremental competitive benefit to 2 from 12. Against the unchanged proposal cost of 6, the payoff from continued support is -4. The coalition accordingly decided to end its support.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition no longer endorses the federal carbon-pricing proposal. The underlying commercial calculations remain private.","candidate_implication":"Researchers should predict that private documents dated immediately before endorsement reversals will contain newly received competitive-position information, whereas the subsequent public notes will report the decision without reproducing that information.","derivation":"The private notice precedes the decision, CA makes competitive benefit causally relevant to support, the memo records the actual decision, and commercial numbers are withheld publicly. These premises jointly predict a temporal and informational documentary pattern.","extra_assumption":"Documents preserve sufficiently precise dates to establish whether the competitive information preceded the decision."}]}
